sentences.text: The deceased plaintiff has filed this suit for partition and separate possession of his legitimate share in 'A' & 'B' schedule properties and also for declaration of Sale Deeds as null and void.
Shorn of unnecessary details, brief version of the parties as projected by them during trial is recapitulated as under;
The father of the plaintiff is Late S.Kupparaju, the defendant Nos.1 and 2 are the sisters of the plaintiff.

The father of the plaintiff S.Kupparaju was the owner and possessor of schedule 'A' & 'B'
properties.
He died on 26-07-1982.
After the death of Kupparaju, the plaintiff and defendants are brought up by their mother Yengamma, at the time of death of Kupparaju, the plaintiff and defendant Nos.1 and 2 were minors.
Therefore, the mother of the plaintiff Yengamma with great difficulty brought up the plaintiff and defendant Nos.1 and 2.
According to the plaintiff, his father S.Kupparaju, purchased the suit schedule properties from his vendor in the year 1952.
The name of Kupparaju entered in the Village Panchayath records.
He was the owner and possessor of schedule 'A' and 'B' properties.
Schedule 'A' & 'B' properties are consisting of the residential houses.
The houses are let out by Yengamma.

Since Yengamma was illiterate and does not have worldly knowledge, she was assisted by the uncle of the plaintiff by name Venkatanarasimha Raju from 1982 to till the death of Yengamma, the uncle of plaintiff,
O.S.No.8206/2012 Venkatanarasimha Raju, managing the suit schedule properties obtaining the rent from the tenants.
The marriages of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 wee performed by Yengamma with the help of Venkatanarasimha Raju out of the rent income derived from the suit schedule properties.
According to the plaintiff, even after the death of Yengamma, the uncle of plaintiff was told to manage the suit schedule property till his death on 6-6-2012.
According to the plaintiff, during the life time of his uncle Venkatanarasimha Raju, he was told by the plaintiff to divide the 'B' schedule property in three parts but it was not materialized.
In the mean time, the original property documents kept in the house of the plaintiff were missing.
The defendant Nos.3 to 7 are the tenants in the suit schedule properties inducted by Venkatanarasimha Raju.
The plaintiff searched the missing property documents in his house and in the suit schedule properties.
Since he was unable to go to the police station, he executed Power of Attorney in favour of the daughter of Venkatanarasimha Raju by name Shyamala.
She asked the defendant Nos.3 to 7 to vacate the suit premises and hand over the vacant possession to her.
By that time, the defendant No.3 and others proclaimed that the defendant O.S.No.8206/2012 No.3 becomes owner and possessor of 'A' & 'B'

Therefore, those documents are not binding on the plaintiff.
Since the properties belonging to his father S.Kupparaju, he is entitled for legitimate share in the suit schedule properties.
Hence, he prays to decree the suit.
3. The suit summons issued to the defendants.
The defendant Nos.1, 2 and 7 are placed exparte.
During the pendency of the suit, the defendant No.6 dead, her L.Rs are not brought on record, no specific order regarding the abatement was passed.
Since no steps taken to bring the L.Rs, suit against the defendant No.6 stands abated.
4. The defendant Nos.3 to 5 appeared through their counsel.
The defendant No.3 by name Sampathraju filed written statement.
He denied the plaint averments in toto.
He claims that he is he bonafide purchaser of the suit schedule properties.
'A' schedule property is purchased by him on 20-06-2001, 'B' schedule property was purchased by him on 29-01-2024.
According to him, these properties are de-notified in his name and in the name of Challamma.
'A' schedule property was regularized in his name by virtue of Order dated 10-06-2004 by BDA.
The price fixed by the O.S.No.8206/2012 BDA was paid by the plaintiff.
His ownership and possession was confirmed on 14-06-2004.
He obtained building license to construct building on 'A' schedule property on 12-10-2004.
After completion of the building, katha certificate was issued by BBMP on 25-09-2006.
Therefore, he is in peaceful possession and enjoyment of 'A' schedule property from the date of purchase to till the date of filing of the written statement.
5. The defendant No.3 contended that 'B' schedule property previously belonging to Challamma, it was de-notified in her name as per Order dated 22-10-1998 by BDA.
Katha Certificate was issued by BDA on 24-03-1999.
The defendant No.3 has purchased 'B' schedule property on 29-01-2004 by Challamma.
Thereafter, obtained building plan on 25-09-2006.

He constructed the house in 'B'
schedule property.
'B' schedule property is also in his possession.

The defendant No.3 filed additional written statement wherein, he took the plea that the suit filed by the plaintiff is barred by limitation, suit is bad for non-joinder and misjoinder of parties and the Court fee paid by plaintiff is not sufficient.
Hence, the defendant No.3 sought to dismiss the suit.

sentences.text: The plaintiff is not in possession either joint or exclusive over the suit schedule properties.

The defendant No.3 able to prove that he is the bonafide purchaser of the suit schedule properties, elaborate cross-examination of D.W.1 was conducted by the Advocate for plaintiff but nothing helpful to the case of plaintiffs O.S.No.8206/2012 elicited during the cross-examination.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 in affirmative.

27. Issue No.3:- The defendant No.5 claimed that the defendant No.3 has played fraud on her, entire sale consideration was not paid while obtaining the Sale Deed on 29-11-2000 in respect of 'A'
schedule property.
But, she did not enter the witness box not substantiated her stand.
Therefore, I answer issue No.3 in negative.

28. Issue No.4:- The plaintiff clearly stated the cause of action for filing this suit in para No.16 of the plaint, the defendant No.3 merely denied that there is no cause of action for filing the suit.
No-doubt, the plaintiff was not able to prove the fraud and misrepresentation.
But he fact is that he filed the suit on the notion that he is entitled for share in it.
Therefore, there is cause of action for filing the suit.
Hence, I answer issue No.4 in affirmative.
29. Issue No.5 & Addl.issue No.3:- These two issues are in respect of in adequacy of Court fee.

According to learned counsel for the defendant No.3, during the pendency of the suit, the plaint O.S.No.8206/2012 was amended, additional prayers were incorporated to declare the Sale Deeds,
dated 29-11-2000, 21-6-2001 and 29-1-2004 are null and void and not binding on him.
Since the partition is the comprehensive relief, he need not seek for cancellation of Sale Deed, only the relief of not binding is sufficient.
The valuation made by the plaintiff is proper and sufficient and substantial Court Fee is paid.
Therefore, I answer issue No.5 and additional issue No.3 in negative.

Issue Nos.1 and 2:-
The defendant No.3 contended that the suit is barred by limitation.
In this regard, he contended that the execution of GPA, Sale Deeds dated 29-11-2000 and 29-1-2004 are known to the entire world.
Limitation begins to run from the date of documents referred above and he referred about Article 58 of the Limitation Act.
31. Apart from it, the evidence of the P.W.1 coupled with Exs.P.67 to P.94 demonstrates that the Sy.No.21 of Thayappanahalli was acquired by CITB in the year 1947.
Out of it, 5 guntas was de-notified in the year 1952.
An application was filed by the defendant No.3 and Challamma for regularisation of their illegal O.S.No.8206/2012 occupation over 5 guntas of land.
The regularization of Challamma's property was made on 22-10-1998 and regularization of 'A' schedule property in favour of defendant No.3 was made on 14-06-2004.
In both properties, the defendant No.3 has constructed building in the year 2004-06 respectively.
The suit came to be filed in the year 2012.
Therefore, the suit filed by the plaintiff is barred by limitation.
32. The defendant No.3 also took contention that a fraud has been alleged against the defendant Nos.3 to 7 but N.Chayarani who claims to be the GPA holder of deceased Kupparaju was not made as party.
It clearly goes to show that the suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Hence, I answer additional issue No.1 in affirmative, additional issue No.2 partly in affirmative.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The deceased plaintiff has filed this suit for partition and separate possession of his legitimate share in 'A' & 'B' schedule properties and also for declaration of Sale Deeds as null and void.
The father of the plaintiff S.Kupparaju was the owner and possessor of schedule 'A' & 'B'
properties.
He died on 26-07-1982.
After the death of Kupparaju, the plaintiff and defendants are brought up by their mother Yengamma, at the time of death of Kupparaju, the plaintiff and defendant Nos.1 and 2 were minors.
Therefore, the mother of the plaintiff Yengamma with great difficulty brought up the plaintiff and defendant Nos.1 and 2.
According to the plaintiff, his father S.Kupparaju, purchased the suit schedule properties from his vendor in the year 1952.
He was the owner and possessor of schedule 'A' and 'B' properties.
The marriages of the defendant Nos.1 and 2 wee performed by Yengamma with the help of Venkatanarasimha Raju out of the rent income derived from the suit schedule properties.
The defendant Nos.3 to 7 are the tenants in the suit schedule properties inducted by Venkatanarasimha Raju.
The plaintiff searched the missing property documents in his house and in the suit schedule properties.
She asked the defendant Nos.3 to 7 to vacate the suit premises and hand over the vacant possession to her.
Hence, based on fraudulent GPA, the defendant No.3 in collusion with defendant Nos.4 & 5 created Sale Deed on 29-11-2000 in respect of 'A'
schedule property.
Similarly, the defendant No.3 created another Sale Deed dated 29-1-2004 in collusion with the other defendants.
According to the plaintiff, he and defendant Nos.1 and 2 are in joint possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property, the Sale Deeds and other documents are created by fraud and O.S.No.8206/2012 misrepresentation.
Since the properties belonging to his father S.Kupparaju, he is entitled for legitimate share in the suit schedule properties.
During the pendency of the suit, the defendant No.6 dead, her L.Rs are not brought on record, no specific order regarding the abatement was passed.
He obtained building license to construct building on 'A' schedule property on 12-10-2004.
Thereafter, obtained building plan on 25-09-2006.
He constructed the house in 'B'
schedule property.
The defendant No.3 filed additional written statement wherein, he took the plea that the suit filed by the plaintiff is barred by limitation, suit is bad for non-joinder and misjoinder of parties and the Court fee paid by plaintiff is not sufficient.
Hence, the defendant No.3 sought to dismiss the suit.
'A' schedule property was purchased by her from GPA holder of Puttaraju by virtue of the registered GPA dated 29-11-2000.
Subsequently, the defendant No.3 negotiated with her to purchase the 'A' schedule property for consideration of .8,000/-.
But, he has not paid entire sale consideration to her and she is entitled to recover .2,00,000/- from defendant No.3 as balance sale consideration amount.
However, on assurance of the defendant No.3, she executed Sale Deed in respect of 'A' schedule property on 20-06-2001.
She reserved her right to recover  2,00,000/- from defendant No.3.
opennyai_summary.issue:
7. Based on the pleadings, my Predecessor in office has framed the following issues:-
1. Whether plaintiffs prove plaint schedule properties of him and defendants 1 and 2 O.S.No.8206/2012 are joint family properties?
2.
Whether defendant No.3 proves he is he bonafide purchaser of plaint 'A' and 'B'
schedule properties?
3. Whether 5rh defendant has got a claim against 3rd defendant for recovery of balance consideration amount?
4. Whether there is a cause of action for the suit?
5. Whether 3rd defendant proves the suit is not properly valued?
6. To what relief the plaintiffs are entitled for?
7.
What Order
/ Decree?
Additional issues framed on 13-09-2022 1.
Whether defendant No.3 proves that the suit is barred by limitation?
2. Whether defendant No.3 proves that the suit is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and mis-joinder of unnecessary parties?
3. Whether defendant No.3 proves that the Court fee paid by the plaintiffs is not proper and correct?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It was decreed holding that the defendant No.3 is in possession and enjoyment of 'B' schedule property.
No complaint was filed regarding missing of original documents.
The acquisition made by the BDA was within the exclusive knowledge of plaintiff, regularization of 'A' schedule property, execution of the GPA in favour of N.Chayarani is also in the exclusive knowledge of the plaintiff.
The plaintiff is not in possession either joint or exclusive over the suit schedule properties.
No-doubt, the plaintiff was not able to prove the fraud and misrepresentation.
But he fact is that he filed the suit on the notion that he is entitled for share in it.
Therefore, there is cause of action for filing the suit.
Since the partition is the comprehensive relief, he need not seek for cancellation of Sale Deed, only the relief of not binding is sufficient.
The defendant No.3 contended that the suit is barred by limitation.
Out of it, 5 guntas was de-notified in the year 1952.
The regularization of Challamma's property was made on 22-10-1998 and regularization of 'A' schedule property in favour of defendant No.3 was made on 14-06-2004.
The suit came to be filed in the year 2012.
Therefore, the suit filed by the plaintiff is barred by limitation.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The learned counsel for the plaintiff drew my attention to Ex.P.30 which is the certified copy of General Power of Attorney alleged to have been executed by S.Kupparaju in favour of N.Chayarani.
According to the learned counsel for the plaintiff,
S.Kupparaju died in the year 1982 how he can execute the PA in favour of N.Chayarani.
His argument is that this GPA is created by defendant No.3 to grab 'A' schedule property.

Hence, he is not entitled for any relief claimed in the plaint.

O.S.No.8206/2012 ORDER Suit of the plaintiff dismissed with costs.
